business_problem: Datasite needed a more scalable and developer-controlled platform for virtual data rooms and document-heavy M&A workflows than a relational database could provide.
solution_summary: Datasite moved the heart of its M&A document platform from a relational database to MongoDB, first with Enterprise Advanced and then with MongoDB Atlas, so engineers could manage massive document sets in a way that matched how the application actually works. Atlas stores uploaded deal documents, folder structures, row-level tracker data, and related metadata for virtual data rooms that often contain hundreds of thousands of files. Because engineers control schema and indexing directly, the team can iterate faster on features such as Trackers, cloning, and AI-assisted imports while Atlas absorbs platform-management work. That combination delivers sub-50ms queries, faster feature delivery, and a more resilient CI/CD model for a business supporting dealmakers in more than 180 countries.
